name: Data Centre
short_description: Mission-critical engineering & construction for colocation, hyperscale and HPC-ready facilities.
long_description: Unique Engineers has delivered MEPF for data centres including STT GDC Mumbai (9 MW, ₹32 Cr), CtrlS Mahape (20 MW, Rated-4, ₹80 Cr) and Digital Edge BOM01 (48 MW, seismic-detailed, ₹50 Cr) — with further engagements for Anant Raj Cloud and STPI. Tier-3 / Tier-4 ready topologies are engineered across mechanical, electrical, fire and BMS, verified in commissioning. Every facility is built around concurrent maintainability, ASHRAE TC 9.9 supply-air management, and a clear migration path to liquid cooling for AI/HPC density.
hero_image_alt: Data centre white-space hot-aisle interior with server racks

sections.heading: White-space cooling
body: Air-side strategy is settled at design: hot/cold-aisle containment, perimeter CRAH and InRow cooling for medium-density halls, rear-door heat exchangers for high-density rows, and reserved liquid manifolds for the migration to AI/HPC density.

Supply-air temperature is managed to ASHRAE TC 9.9 with the operator's risk tolerance. Free-cooling hours are calculated against the site's wet-bulb profile; chiller staging, pump VFDs and tower fan VFDs are sequenced for low part-load energy.

systems.name: Aisle containment & SAT management
systems.description: Hot- or cold-aisle containment with brush seals and blanking panels. Supply-air temperature monitored to ASHRAE TC 9.9 across every aisle.

systems.name: CRAH / InRow / RDHX
systems.description: Perimeter CRAH for general halls, InRow for medium-high density, rear-door HX for AI/HPC zones up to 30 kW/rack.

systems.name: Liquid-ready architecture
systems.description: Reserved liquid manifolds and CDU drops for non-disruptive migration to direct liquid cooling.

sections.heading: Critical power & MEP redundancy
body: HV → LV → UPS → IT load engineered for fault-tolerant uptime. 33/22/11 kV HT systems, transformers, LV switchgear, busbar trunking and cable distribution — all topology choices driven by the operator's Tier rating.
DG sets sized for full IT + cooling block load; modular static UPS with ventilated battery rooms and BMS-integrated H₂ sensing. Earthing, harmonic mitigation and TVSS specified end-to-end.

systems.name: HV / LV distribution
systems.description: 33/22/11 kV HT, transformers, LV switchgear, busbar trunking. Main-tie-main and ring topologies per spec.

systems.name: Diesel generation
systems.description: Full block-load DG sizing, day + bulk fuel, UL-certified polishing skids, explosion-proof control.

systems.name: UPS & battery rooms
systems.description: Modular static UPS, ventilated battery rooms, BMS-integrated H₂ sensing, concurrent-maintainable bypass.

sections.heading: BMS · IBMS · DCIM integration
body: Unified controls plane — every plant, every alarm, every event in one place. Field DDC across HVAC, electrical, fire and security; head-end SCADA + historian; real-time operator dashboards with role-based alarm hierarchy.

Open Modbus / BACnet / SNMP feeds into the operator's DCIM. Standardised tag dictionary signed off pre-commissioning; joint witness on BMS-DCIM integration tests so the operator inherits a working system, not a vendor lock-in.

sections.heading: Tier-3 / Tier-4 readiness
body: Designed to Uptime Institute Tier topology. Concurrent maintainability and (for Tier IV) fault-tolerant topologies engineered across mechanical, electrical, fire and BMS — verified in the commissioning protocol.

Annual outage allowance ≤ 1.6 hr for Tier III and ≤ 0.4 hr for Tier IV. SPOF audit at design freeze and at every change-control event. 2-hour fire-rated MEP / electrical / battery compartments, pen-sealed and witnessed.

sections.heading: Commissioning · L1 → L5
body: Aligned to Uptime Institute Cx and ASHRAE / AABC / NEBB protocols. L1 component verification, L2 static testing, L3 component start-up, L4 integrated systems test, L5 performance and operational under load.

Each level signed off — operator-witnessed where required — before the next is initiated. Handover dossier includes as-built drawings, federated BIM model, equipment datasheets, IOM manuals, TAB reports, NABL-traceable calibration certificates, training records and fire-authority NOC.

name: Semiconductor & Cleanroom
short_description: Cleanroom MEPF, process gases and high-precision utilities for semiconductor fabs and solar-cell manufacturing.
long_description: Active across India's semiconductor frontier — Foxconn (Apple) in Bangalore (₹650+ Cr across 10+ work packages), Tata Electronics at Dholera and Assam, and the SAEL solar-cell facility at Jewar (5.75 GW, 66,000 sqm of ISO 6/7/8 cleanroom, 29,250 TR of process cooling). Class 10K/100K (ISO 7/8) executed at scale, with the engineering delta to ISO 6 fully understood. CDA, nitrogen, vacuum and PCW networks delivered with strict slope control, leak-tested to stringent standards, integrated without compromising contamination zones.
hero_image_alt: Semiconductor cleanroom interior with FFU array and fab equipment

sections.heading: Cleanroom credentials
body: Class 10,000 / 100,000 (ISO 7 / 8) executed at scale for Foxconn (Apple) in Bangalore — wall and ceiling PUF panelling, epoxy flooring, HEPA-filtered AHUs, return-air risers, cleanroom doors and view panels.

Engineering delta to ISO 6 fully understood: higher air change rates (60-90 ACPH vs 20-40 for ISO 7/8), semi/fully-directional airflow with FFU assistance, HEPA H13/H14 terminal filtration in gel-seal housings with in-situ leak testing, tighter pressure cascade (≥15 Pa between zones), controlled return-air architecture with low-level returns for particle sweep-out, and ±1 °C / ±5% RH stability.

systems.name: PUF panel cleanroom
systems.description: Wall + ceiling PUF panelling, epoxy flooring, HEPA-filtered AHUs, return-air risers, cleanroom doors and view panels.

systems.name: FFU array (HEPA H13/H14)
systems.description: Ceiling-grid FFU layout with terminal HEPA filtration. 13,656 FFUs installed at SAEL alone.

systems.name: Process gas distribution
systems.description: CDA, N₂ and Vacuum networks routed with strict slope control, leak-tested to stringent standards. SS / aluminium / electropolished as spec demands.

sections.heading: Process cooling water
body: Closed-loop SS 316 / PP-H PCW networks with primary-secondary distribution, plate heat exchanger isolation, conductivity and leak taps for real-time monitoring, OEM-validated POU hookups. Delivered for Foxconn India, JSW EV battery-line cooling, and the SAEL solar-cell facility (dual 5.05 MW SS316 PHE).
Hydronics design follows ASME B31.3 with hydro and pneumatic testing on every closed loop. Welding qualified to ASME IX with continuous third-party inspection on critical joints.

sections.heading: Active portfolio momentum
body: Tata Semiconductor (Assam) — utility HVAC for the upcoming fab; Tata Semiconductor (Dholera) — 3 packages awarded, expansion expected toward ₹500 Cr; JSW EV (Bangalore) — full MEPF including ISO 7/8 battery-assembly cleanroom; Foxconn (Bangalore) — PLC + BMS integration across the existing controlled-environment estate.
Each engagement brings a different cleanroom or process requirement — the experience compounds across the portfolio.

name: Industrial & Manufacturing
short_description: Factory floors, manufacturing halls and process plants for automotive, FMCG, electronics and heavy industry.
long_description: Industrial MEPF delivered for JSW EV manufacturing, Coca-Cola plants, Unilever, BMW, ITC, Hyundai and the IKEA Noida mixed-use development. Single-window design-build engagements keep engineering, installation and commissioning under one coordinated delivery team.
hero_image_alt: Modern automotive factory floor with robotic assembly equipment

sections.heading: Why design-build for industrial
body: One contract covers design and execution. The same team that engineered the system installs and commissions it — no design-vs-build finger-pointing, no clarification loops, no translation losses between architect, MEP consultant and contractor.

Design and execution can overlap rather than wait for a fully sequential release. Long-lead procurement starts when the relevant design intent freezes, while value engineering remains focused at the design stage, before change becomes disruptive on site.

sections.heading: Sector breadth
body: Active across automotive (JSW EV, MG Motor, BMW, Hyundai), FMCG (Coca-Cola, Unilever, ITC), district cooling (Tabreed Amravati — 30,000 TR), and mixed-use industrial (IKEA Noida — ₹411 Cr).

Delivery experience spans the firm's national project record, with project teams organised around the specific work fronts, plant interfaces, commissioning sequence and handover requirements of each facility.

sections.heading: Engineering depth
body: Thermal, hydraulic, electrical and coordination models are developed against the facility load, equipment interfaces and maintainability requirements, then translated into coordinated shop drawings and work packages.
Inspection and test plans, material traceability, pre-commissioning checks, integrated testing and the final handover dossier establish a documented path from design intent to operating system.

name: Airport & Public Venues
short_description: Full-scope MEPF for airports, stadiums and large public-venue infrastructure under compressed timelines.
long_description: Delivered full MEPF for Mopa (Manohar) International Airport in Goa — ₹130 Cr, LEED-aligned — plus CWG stadiums and hotels. Pre-fabrication strategies and parallel work fronts hold schedule discipline through compressed airport-construction windows. Empanelled with AAI for civil-aviation infrastructure.
hero_image_alt: Modern airport terminal interior with sweeping curved roof

sections.heading: Operationally critical public infrastructure
body: Airport and large public-venue systems are planned around passenger flow, security zoning, fire strategy, baggage and retail interfaces, long operating hours and the staged release of public areas.

The MEPF programme is divided into coordinated work fronts so plantrooms, concourses, airside areas and back-of-house zones can move through installation, inspection and commissioning without losing interface control.

systems.name: Terminal HVAC
systems.description: Central plants, air distribution, ventilation and controls coordinated for varying occupancy, solar load and operating schedules.

systems.name: Life-safety systems
systems.description: Fire detection, hydrant, sprinkler, smoke-control and emergency-power interfaces verified through cause-and-effect testing.

systems.name: Public-area utilities
systems.description: Electrical, plumbing and specialist service routes coordinated around architecture, passenger circulation and maintainable access.

sections.heading: Interface-led construction
body: Builder's-work drawings, penetration schedules, ceiling coordination and equipment-access studies are closed before installation fronts are released.
Prefabricated assemblies and repeatable modules are used where the design, transport route and lifting plan support them, reducing congestion and improving repeatability on site.

sections.heading: Integrated testing and handover
body: Commissioning moves from component checks to system proving and integrated scenarios, with testing records linked to assets and locations.
Operator demonstrations, training, as-built information and closure of snags are planned as part of the delivery programme—not left to the final weeks.

name: Education & Research
short_description: Universities, schools and research institutes — including India's first net-zero university campus.
long_description: Delivered Nalanda University (Rajgir, ₹60 Cr) — India's first net-zero university campus with geothermal VRV, thermal storage, brine chillers and IBMS. Active across IIT campuses, BITS Pilani, Amity University, South Asian University and Shiv Nadar School.
hero_image_alt: Modern university campus exterior at dusk

sections.heading: Campus-scale engineering
body: Universities and research campuses combine teaching blocks, laboratories, residences, auditoria, kitchens, utilities and landscape infrastructure—each with a different load profile and operating calendar.
Distribution is planned at campus scale while buildings remain independently controllable, maintainable and metered. Phasing anticipates future blocks and limits disruption to occupied facilities.

systems.name: Central and distributed cooling
systems.description: Central plants, VRF, ventilation and specialist environmental control selected by building use, diversity and operating hours.

systems.name: Laboratory and research utilities
systems.description: Exhaust, make-up air, pressure control, power quality and specialist service routes coordinated with laboratory planning.

systems.name: Campus monitoring
systems.description: Metering, BMS integration and operator interfaces structured by building, utility and maintainable asset.

sections.heading: High-performance campus systems
body: Nalanda University's combination of geothermal VRV, thermal storage, brine chillers and integrated controls demonstrates how unconventional systems require the same discipline in hydraulic design, sequencing, testing and operator training as conventional plant.
Energy intent is protected through submittal review, coordinated installation, controls narratives, functional testing and a complete operating record.

sections.heading: Delivery in live learning environments
body: For occupied campuses, shutdowns, temporary services, noisy work and access routes are coordinated around academic calendars and building users.
Handover is structured building by building so campus engineering teams receive usable asset records, training and closed defect lists.

name: Corporate & Retail
short_description: Corporate towers, retail malls and mixed-use developments — including UEL's largest single-order mandate.
long_description: Delivered the Ingka Centre (IKEA) in Noida — a ₹411 Cr mixed-use mandate covering MEPF, solar and PNG. Active across Elan, Bharti Enterprises, Vatika, Spaze, KJL and other developer-led mandates.
hero_image_alt: Premium corporate office tower atrium lobby interior

sections.heading: Mixed-use systems, coordinated as one estate
body: Corporate and retail developments combine offices, public circulation, food and beverage, parking, service yards and sometimes hospitality within one operating estate.
Central utilities and life-safety systems are coordinated with tenant boundaries, landlord provisions, energy metering and phased fit-out requirements from the start.

systems.name: Central utilities
systems.description: Cooling, electrical and water infrastructure sized and sequenced around diversified loads, resilience and phased occupation.

systems.name: Tenant and landlord interfaces
systems.description: Clear demarcation, metering, isolation and fit-out connection points reduce rework as tenant packages evolve.

systems.name: Public-realm life safety
systems.description: Fire alarm, suppression, smoke control, emergency power and evacuation interfaces coordinated across shared and leased spaces.

sections.heading: Commercial programme control
body: Equipment approvals, long-lead procurement, riser and ceiling coordination and builder's-work requirements are managed against area-release dates.
Zone-based work fronts allow commissioning and handover to follow the development's opening sequence rather than waiting for a single final completion event.

sections.heading: Operational readiness
body: Controls graphics, metering, fire cause-and-effect, water balancing, electrical testing and equipment demonstrations are integrated into the handover plan.
Asset data, warranties, training records and as-built information are organised so the facilities team can operate a complex multi-tenant estate from day one.

name: Healthcare
short_description: Hospitals, healthcare campuses and multi-specialty facilities with stringent infection-control HVAC.
long_description: Healthcare MEPF delivered across AIIMS, CGHS, Lady Hardinge Medical College and other multi-specialty hospitals. HVAC engineered for operating-theatre pressure cascade, isolation rooms, and AIIMS-grade infection-control standards. NCR hospital O&M maintained continuously through the pandemic.
hero_image_alt: Modern hospital corridor interior with clinical lighting

sections.heading: Clinical environmental control
body: Hospitals require environmental control by clinical risk: operating theatres, isolation rooms, critical care, diagnostics, wards, laboratories and public areas each demand a defined pressure, filtration and ventilation response.
Room data, pressure relationships, heat loads, air-change requirements and maintainable filter access are coordinated before ductwork and terminal layouts are released.

systems.name: Operating theatres
systems.description: Dedicated air systems, terminal filtration, pressure cascade, temperature and humidity control with room-by-room verification.

systems.name: Isolation and critical care
systems.description: Supply, extract, pressure monitoring and alarm interfaces coordinated to the clinical infection-control strategy.

systems.name: Essential services
systems.description: Emergency power, fire-life-safety, water, drainage and controls planned around continuity of clinical operation.

sections.heading: Construction in sensitive facilities
body: In live hospitals, work zones, dust control, shutdowns, temporary services and infection-control measures are planned with the hospital team before access is released.
Testing and energisation are sequenced to protect critical departments and maintain clear rollback provisions for every planned interruption.

sections.heading: Validation and documented handover
body: Air and water balancing, HEPA integrity where specified, pressure testing, electrical verification, fire-system testing and BMS trending establish that the installed system performs as designed.
Room-level records, calibration evidence, approved drawings, asset schedules and operator training form the basis of clinical handover.

name: Hospitality
short_description: Five-star hotels and resort campuses — guest-room conditioning, banqueting, kitchens, spa and back-of-house.
long_description: Delivered HVAC and MEPF for five-star hotel campuses — Westin, Marriott, Radisson, Crowne Plaza, Holiday Inn and Palazzo. Four-pipe FCU systems for guest rooms, DOAS make-up, specialist treatment for ballrooms, kitchens and spa zones. Acoustic-led selection in occupied areas.
hero_image_alt: Luxury five-star hotel grand lobby with marble atrium

sections.heading: Comfort that disappears into the experience
body: Hotel systems must deliver quiet, stable comfort while remaining accessible to the engineering team and unobtrusive to the guest.
Room-module coordination aligns fan-coil units, fresh air, drainage, fire protection, power, controls and ceiling access before repetitive floors move into production.

systems.name: Guest-room conditioning
systems.description: FCU, VRF or DX solutions selected around acoustic criteria, control response, ventilation and maintainability.

systems.name: Ballrooms and public areas
systems.description: High-diversity cooling, fresh air and controls planned around changing occupancy and event loads.

systems.name: Kitchens, laundry and spa
systems.description: Specialist exhaust, make-up air, hot water, drainage and humidity control coordinated with operating equipment.

sections.heading: Repetition with quality control
body: Approved room mock-ups establish routing, access, acoustic treatment, insulation finish, controls and testing criteria before the typical-floor sequence begins.
Floor-by-floor inspection and progressive testing make quality visible early and prevent defects from repeating across the room inventory.

sections.heading: Commissioning for opening day
body: Guest rooms, kitchens, public areas and central plant are commissioned against the hotel's operational zoning and phased opening plan.
Seasonal settings, operator training, asset data and maintenance access are resolved before areas move into guest use.

name: Residential
short_description: Premium and luxury residential developments — guest-room HVAC, plumbing, electrical and BMS at residential scale.
long_description: Delivered MEPF for premium residential mandates — M3M, DLF, Sky Mansion, Vatika, Suncity and Elan. VRF heat-recovery, four-pipe FCU and split DX selected per the building's acoustic and ventilation budget.
hero_image_alt: Premium high-rise luxury residential tower at dusk

sections.heading: High-rise residential infrastructure
body: Residential towers require services to work quietly, reliably and repeatedly across hundreds of homes while common-area plant remains accessible to the facilities team.
Risers, pressure zones, electrical distribution, fire strategy, ventilation and apartment interfaces are coordinated with structure, façades and interior layouts before typical floors accelerate.

systems.name: Water and drainage zoning
systems.description: Pressure breaks, pumping, storage, hot-water and drainage systems planned for tower height, simultaneity and maintainable isolation.

systems.name: Apartment comfort
systems.description: VRF, FCU or DX conditioning coordinated for acoustic performance, ventilation, condensate and service access.

systems.name: Common-area safety
systems.description: Fire protection, smoke management, emergency power and detection integrated across towers, basements and amenity spaces.

sections.heading: Typical-floor production control
body: A coordinated apartment and corridor mock-up sets the standard for supports, sleeves, shafts, ceiling zones, access panels and final finish.
Repeatable inspection checkpoints, pressure tests and concealed-work records keep quality consistent as multiple towers and floors advance in parallel.

sections.heading: Tower-by-tower handover
body: Plant, risers, apartments and common areas move through progressive pre-commissioning before integrated tests and authority inspections.
Asset schedules, warranties, test records, as-built drawings and operator training are organised by tower and system for practical facilities management.
